title: Context Contract
description: The conditions under which an agent is INTENDED to operate. Held separately from the Agent Passport because the two change independently: the same build moved into a different business context is as much a new decision as a new build in the same context. A Passport says what the agent can do; a Contract says what it is permitted to do. Comparing them mechanically catches divergence — usually a tool added without revisiting the contract — which no runtime monitoring surfaces, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

purpose.description: Business purpose. Assurance is context-specific; without a purpose there is no context to assure against.

affected_parties.description: People who bear consequences without choosing to use the agent.

prohibited_actions.description: Red lines. A capability the agent actually holds that appears here is a demonstrated breach, which caps the recommendation at reject. A contract declaring nothing prohibited cannot produce a breach, and is more likely incomplete than permissive.

required_human_oversight.description: Action classes needing human confirmation. If this is non-empty and the Passport records no review workflow, the control the approval depends on is absent — a breach rather than a gap.

stop_conditions.description: Conditions under which operation must stop, stated in advance rather than judged during an incident.
